git_status.rationale: `Shows the working tree status` for a `repo_path`, so it can return non-public host repository metadata such as paths/statuses from the local working tree (SECRET). Status text may include filenames or branch names from a repository whose contents/names could be authored by third parties; the advertised text does not state the repository is only user-authored, so UNTRUSTED is kept under the least-restrictive reading.

git_diff_unstaged.rationale: `Shows changes in the working directory that are not yet staged` for a `repo_path`, so it can return non-public host file contents/diffs from the working directory (SECRET). Diff content and paths may come from third-party-authored repository files or changes; the description does not rule that out, so UNTRUSTED is kept.

git_diff_staged.rationale: `Shows changes that are staged for commit` for a `repo_path`, so it can return non-public staged host file contents/diffs (SECRET). Staged diff text and file paths may include content authored by third parties in a multi-writer repository; the description does not settle authorship, so UNTRUSTED is kept.

git_diff.rationale: `Shows differences between branches or commits` in a local `repo_path`, so it can return non-public repository contents from host storage (SECRET). Branches or commits can contain third-party-authored code, paths, and commit data; since the advertised text does not constrain the repository to trusted authors, UNTRUSTED is kept.

git_commit.rationale: `Records changes to the repository`, which changes local repository state but is not advertised as sending data to an attacker-readable destination or returning non-public data. The `message` is agent-supplied content stored in the local repository, not a public sink from the advertised text.

git_add.rationale: `Adds file contents to the staging area`, which changes local repository/index state. It is not advertised as returning file contents or sending data to an external/public destination.

git_reset.rationale: `Unstages all staged changes`, which changes local repository/index state. It is not advertised as returning secrets, fetching attacker-controlled content, or sending data out.

git_log.rationale: `Shows the commit logs` for a `repo_path`, so it can reveal non-public local repository history, commit IDs, messages, authors, and timestamps (SECRET). Commit messages, author names, branch/history data may be third-party-authored in a multi-writer repository; the description does not restrict authorship, so UNTRUSTED is kept.

git_create_branch.rationale: `Creates a new branch from an optional base branch`, which changes local repository branch state. It is not advertised as returning non-public data or delivering agent-supplied data to an attacker-readable destination.

git_checkout.rationale: `Switches branches`, which changes local working tree/repository state. It is not advertised as returning secrets or sending data out.

git_show.rationale: `Shows the contents of a commit` for a local `repo_path`, so it can return non-public repository file contents and commit metadata (SECRET). Commit contents/messages/paths may be authored by third parties; the description does not rule this out, so UNTRUSTED is kept.

git_branch.rationale: `List Git branches` for a `repo_path`, including `remote branches ('remote') or all branches('all')`, so it can reveal non-public local/remote branch names known to the repository (SECRET). Remote branch names can be created by other parties and are attacker-controllable in multi-writer repositories, so UNTRUSTED applies.

notes: No output schemas are advertised; where a tool description says it shows or lists Git data, `return` is used for output field classifications. Local Git writes are treated as state changes but not SINKs because the advertised tools do not push or publish to an attacker-readable destination.
